setup: The user has installed the PDF split and merge application and has a source PDF file saved in a local folder. The original PDF is closed in any other editor and is available only as an input file.
action: The user opens the PDF in the graphical tool, performs a document manipulation task, and saves the result with a new output name.
expected_observation: The application provides a graphical interface for PDF manipulation, and the original input PDF remains unchanged on disk after the task completes.

setup: The user has a multi-page PDF document loaded into the graphical tool and can preview its pages.
action: The user chooses the split function and specifies that pages 1-3 should be saved as one file and pages 4 onward as another file.
expected_observation: The tool creates separate PDF output files according to the chosen split points, and each output contains only the expected page range.

setup: The user has two or more PDF files, or selected page sections from PDFs, available in the workspace.
action: The user selects the files or sections to merge and confirms the merge operation.
expected_observation: The tool produces one combined PDF in the selected order, containing all chosen files or sections as a single document.

setup: The user has opened a PDF document with multiple pages and can view page thumbnails or page numbers.
action: The user selects a subset of pages to extract and runs the extract-pages operation.
expected_observation: The tool generates a new PDF containing only the selected pages, and the unselected pages are not included in the extracted file.

setup: The user has loaded a PDF document with pages that need orientation changes, and page previews are visible.
action: The user rotates one or more selected pages by 90 degrees and confirms the change.
expected_observation: The selected pages appear in the new orientation in the resulting PDF, while unselected pages keep their original orientation.

setup: The user has opened a PDF document with pages displayed in thumbnail order.
action: The user drags pages into a different sequence and then exports the document.
expected_observation: The output PDF reflects the new page order exactly as arranged by the user.

setup: The user has two source PDFs with pages that should be interleaved, and both documents are loaded in the tool.
action: The user selects alternating pages from the two documents and merges them in an interleaved pattern.
expected_observation: The resulting PDF alternates pages from the selected documents in the chosen sequence, such as A1, B1, A2, B2, without dropping selected pages.

setup: The user is working in the visual composition workspace with page thumbnails from one or more PDFs available for layout.
action: The user arranges selected pages visually on the composition canvas and generates a new document.
expected_observation: The tool creates a new PDF that matches the visual layout and page composition shown in the workspace.

setup: The user has a PDF task that must be repeated later, and the command-line interface is available on the system.
action: The user runs a command-line operation that applies a PDF split, merge, or extract task using saved parameters.
expected_observation: The tool completes the task without opening the graphical interface and produces the expected output, enabling automated or repeatable use.

setup: The user has configured a preferred workspace state, including open documents, selected pages, or recent task settings.
action: The user saves the current setup and later reloads it from the tool's saved environments or session list.
expected_observation: The previously saved workspace state is restored, including the relevant documents, selections, and task settings available at the time of saving.

setup: The user has a standard-sized PDF document and is ready to perform a manipulation task on a typical workstation.
action: The user starts a PDF split, merge, or page arrangement operation and requests the result.
expected_observation: The tool completes the manipulation promptly enough for interactive use, with no long blocking delay that prevents the user from continuing work.

setup: A user who needs to perform a one-time PDF task opens the application for the first time on a workstation with no special preparation.
action: The user loads a PDF and begins a simple split, merge, or extract operation using the graphical interface.
expected_observation: The interface is straightforward to navigate, and the user can complete the task without a complex setup or lengthy configuration steps.

setup: The user has a PDF loaded and needs to make precise page-level edits while verifying the final result before saving.
action: The user makes page selection, rotation, or ordering changes and reviews the preview before confirming export.
expected_observation: The tool shows a clear preview of the resulting document, allowing the user to inspect page-level changes before the output is generated.

setup: The user opens an existing PDF file as input in the tool and prepares to perform a manipulation without changing the source file directly.
action: The user completes the task and saves the result using the default save behavior.
expected_observation: The original PDF remains intact in its original location and filename, and the tool writes the result as a separate output file by default.

setup: The user has loaded one or more PDF files and is ready to export the result of a split, merge, or extract operation.
action: The user accepts the default save option without selecting overwrite for the source file.
expected_observation: The tool creates a new output PDF instead of replacing the input file, and overwriting occurs only if the user explicitly chooses that option.

setup: A regular office user opens the graphical PDF Split and Merge tool and starts a simple one-off split or merge job without changing any advanced destination settings.
action: The user runs the operation using the default save behavior.
expected_observation: The result files are written to the application's default output folder, and the user can see the saved PDFs there without having to choose a custom destination.

setup: A PDF to be processed is already stored in a work folder, and the graphical tool is configured for a workflow where saving alongside the source document is appropriate.
action: The user selects the option to save the output in the same folder as the source file and starts the job.
expected_observation: The generated PDF output appears beside the original source PDF in the same folder, using the chosen workflow's output naming, with no separate destination prompt.

setup: A power user has a reusable workspace profile saved for a repeated PDF job, including a stored output destination or naming rule.
action: The user opens the saved workspace and runs the same job again.
expected_observation: The tool uses the previously saved destination or naming rule automatically, so the output is routed according to the reusable workspace settings without re-entering the path each time.

setup: The graphical tool is about to write output into a folder that already contains a file with the same name as the generated PDF.
action: The user starts the export or save step for that output file.
expected_observation: Before writing the file, the tool displays a clear confirmation dialog warning that an existing file may be replaced and asks the user to confirm or cancel.

setup: The graphical tool is configured for an operation that will generate several PDF files, such as splitting one document into multiple outputs.
action: The user proceeds to the save step for the multi-file operation.
expected_observation: Before any files are written, the tool shows a clear confirmation or review step indicating that multiple output files will be created.

setup: A command-line user prepares a PDF split or merge job for a non-interactive run, without relying on a graphical prompt.
action: The user launches the command without specifying a destination, or alternatively provides a saved setup that contains the destination rule.
expected_observation: The command is accepted only when the destination is explicitly provided in the command or loaded from the saved setup; otherwise the run is rejected with a clear message that the destination is required.

setup: A graphical workflow is configured to produce one or more PDF outputs, and the user has not yet committed the save action.
action: The user opens the output review step before confirming the operation.
expected_observation: The tool shows the full set of output files, including their names and destinations, before anything is saved.

setup: A PDF split operation is selected that will create multiple output files, and the user has access to naming or destination options in the graphical tool.
action: The user assigns a bulk destination or applies a consistent naming pattern, then starts the job.
expected_observation: All generated files follow the same naming pattern or are saved to the chosen common destination in a predictable, consistent way.

setup: A command-line PDF split or merge job is being prepared for execution.
action: The user enters the command with the operation parameters.
expected_observation: The output location and file behavior are already defined before the job starts, so the run does not pause to ask where to save files during execution.

setup: A command-line user needs to control where output files go or how they are named for a PDF job.
action: The user submits the command with either naming pattern arguments, destination rules, or a saved configuration that contains those settings.
expected_observation: The command uses the provided naming or destination rules as part of the run, and the resulting files are saved according to those passed-in or saved settings.

setup: An automated command-line run is started in a non-interactive environment, and the target output file already exists or could be overwritten.
action: The job runs without an explicit overwrite option.
expected_observation: The tool does not stop to ask for interactive confirmation; it fails safely or aborts with a clear overwrite-related message unless an explicit overwrite option was supplied.

setup: A regular office user has a small PDF issue to fix, such as splitting a brief document or merging a few pages, and wants a quick one-off workflow.
action: The user opens the graphical tool and performs the simple PDF fix using the standard workflow.
expected_observation: The tool supports the user's one-time task with a straightforward flow to load the document, choose the operation, and save the result without requiring advanced setup.

setup: A power user or support staff member regularly repeats the same PDF split or merge operation for similar documents.
action: The user saves the workflow settings and runs the same job again on a new document batch.
expected_observation: The tool supports repeated use by preserving the reusable setup, allowing the user to rerun the operation with minimal reconfiguration.

setup: The project documentation and stakeholder model list regular office users and power users/support staff, but no additional business-side stakeholder groups have been confirmed.
action: A reviewer examines the available requirements and stakeholder statements for completeness.
expected_observation: No separate business stakeholder group is identified beyond the stated user groups, and the gap remains open for later confirmation rather than being assumed.
